items.headline: U.S. Futures Mixed Ahead of Key Events; Tech Under Pressure
items.summary: U.S. stock futures showed a mixed performance early Tuesday, following Monday's session where the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.26% but the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite declined by 0.28% and 0.76% respectively. Investors are keenly awaiting Nvidia's earnings report due Wednesday and a speech from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Friday. Geopolitical tensions surrounding new U.S. sanctions on Iran also continue to influence market sentiment.

items.headline: Fed Chair Warsh to Speak Amid Rate Hike Speculation
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh is scheduled to deliver a key speech at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium on Friday, August 28, with increasing pressure on the Fed to address inflation concerns. The FOMC minutes from July 28-29, released August 19, indicated a 9-3 vote to hold rates at 3.5%-3.75%, though some regional presidents favored a hike.

items.headline: Nvidia Earnings Eyed as Major Market Catalyst This Week
items.summary: All eyes are on Nvidia ($NVDA), which is set to report its quarterly earnings on Wednesday, August 26. The report is widely considered the most important market event of the week, with analysts anticipating approximately $92 billion in quarterly revenue and $29 EPS. The AI giant's performance could dictate the next major move for AI-related stocks.

items.headline: U.S. Imposes New Sanctions on Iran, Escalating Geopolitical Tensions
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced new sanctions against Iran on Monday, warning of an 'economic D-Day' aimed at entities financially connected to Tehran. The move is part of an escalated strategy to pressure Iran, contributing to market jitters and causing Iran's currency to hit a record low.

items.headline: Tech Underperforms as Investors Seek Defensive Sectors
items.summary: Monday saw Information Technology as the worst-performing sector, down 1.59%, with semiconductor stocks specifically weakening. In contrast, consumer staples emerged as the top-performing sector, gaining 1.76%, as investors rotated into defensive names amid broader market uncertainty. Energy, Financials, and Healthcare also showed strength in recent trends.

items.summary: Today's economic calendar includes the final German Q2 GDP, German Ifo Expectations for August, and U.S. ADP Employment Change data. These releases could provide further insights into global economic health and labor market conditions.
